data.title: Tankyrase-2 regulates adipocyte differentiation through AMPK/mTOR signaling.
data.authors: Rauch B; Ujlaki G; Poliska S; Murahwa N; Kovacs P; Pettko-Szandtner A; Uray K; Bai P

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Deleting TNKS1 or TNKS2 slows adipocyte differentiation, with inhibited autophagy, AMPK activation and suppressed mTORC1; the TNKS2-knockout defect is rescued by NV-5138 or by LKB1 inhibition, and TNKS2 ADP-ribosylates LKB1 (cell line).
data.abstract_excerpt: Although tankyrases (TNKSs) were originally described as enzymes safeguarding genome integrity, TNKSs are also associated with metabolism and are involved in the differentiation of multiple cell lineages including adipocytes. Here we aimed to understand the role of TNKSs specifically in adipocyte differentiation. We found that the deletion of TNKS1 or TNKS2 decreased the rate of adipocyte differentiation.

extracted_findings.effect: Reduces adipocyte differentiation rate; AMPK activation suppresses mTORC1
